77.t: Unissued Vocalion sides with King Oliver and Lil, "Don't Pan Me"
77.s: Albertson lists three Vocalion sides of late 1926 with Oliver, Lil and possibly Johnny Dodds; she muses about why they were never released and about bootlegging.
77.ch: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
77.q: Other people kind of riffed a little bit on it, stole a little bit from it. See? (Sings) "Don't talk about me -- don't do the things you know are wrong." No, I can't think of it. But anyhow -- that -- but they -- I think they used the same title and did a few different words, but they didn't do the…

77.t: Mike Jackson, Victor sessions in 1927 and Fats Waller on organ
77.s: Pianist-songwriter Mike Jackson sold his songs cheaply; she recorded with him for Victor, and with Fats Waller on pipe organ in Camden in May 1927.
77.ch: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
77.q: Mike Jackson was a piano player, and he wrote a lot of songs. He was in Chicago, Mike Jackson. He wrote a lot of good songs, and I didn't know -- and he never did get any credit for them. I think he sold most all of them for a few dollars.

77.t: Perry Bradford's Mean Four sides in 1926
77.s: Albertson mentions "Don't Forget to Mess Around" and "Heebie-Jeebies"; she recalls the songs but not the group.
77.ch: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
77.q: Perry Bradford's? No. But you can find all that in this thing. Perry Bradford's got all that down.

77.t: 1922 sides, Fletcher Henderson, and the Original Memphis Five
77.s: She does not recall recording with Sam Wooding; she says she was the first Black woman to record with a white band, the Original Memphis Five, and introduced Porter Grainger's "'Tain't Nobody's Business".
77.ch: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
77.q: "Lonesome Monday Morning Blues." Let me see. Who could that be? I don't ever remember having recorded with Sam Wooding. I don't remember. But I know I used to record with Fletcher a lot. I used to record with -- let me see. What other band was that I recorded with that had --

77.t: Black Swan sessions with Fletcher Henderson and discography check
77.s: Albertson goes through her first Black Swan records for Pace and Handy, with Ray's Dreamland Orchestra and Fletcher Henderson, with William Grant Still arranging; New York, May 1921.
77.q: Paramount. Now, wait a minute, I'm ahead of my story, because I had done notes on some recording already for the Black Swan record. That was Pace and Handy.

30.t: Recording with King Oliver while with Duke; never under contract
30.s: He recorded with Oliver for Clarence Williams after joining Duke, and says he was never under contract to Duke, who could fire him at will as in the early days.
30.q: Oh, well, he didn't have any band anymore and I knew the things that he was going to record. He was going to record for Clarence Williams and he asked me to record with him, so I did it.

30.t: The Oliver date that was really for Clarence Williams
30.s: Williams, who Bigard calls a big crook who stole 'Sister Kate' from Piron, could not get Buster Bailey and got Bigard to record on a date he thought was Oliver's.
30.q: He had to pick up men from around New York and -- oh, I think there was a little trombone player I used to know real well. I can't think of his name offhand, so skip him. But it was nothing. It was all Clarence Williams' tunes.

30.t: Ellington sessions of January to March 1928
30.s: Willard reads the discography for 'Bugle Call Rag', 'Take It Easy' and 'Jubilee Stomp'; Bigard says the process allowed only a snare drum, not a bass drum, and recalls the band's personnel.
30.q: Well, they could use only the snare drum. They couldn't use the bass drum.

67.t: Session with Tiny Parham in Chicago
67.s: He played a couple of dates and recorded Um Ta Da Da Da with Tiny Parham, his second recording, without really working with the band.
67.q: Homer Hobson was a cornet player with Al Williams at the time. He may have been in there, he may have been with -- I don't know anyone in that band.

67.t: First recording with Ma Rainey and early recording methods
67.s: He recorded with Ma Rainey in Chicago with Albert Wynn's band in 1926, using a megaphone and wax.
67.q: Oh, yes. I was with Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band when we made that recording. I knew Ma Rainey because I sat in the Bijou Theater playing shows with the pit band. I wasn’t getting paid, I did it because they let me do it. And I just did it to try to learn as much as I could. And Ma Rainey, she…

611.t: Which King Oliver recording sessions was he on?
611.s: Schaap reads out Oliver dates; Waters recalls six sessions mostly at QRS on Long Island and remembers only 'Snag It', insisting the discographies are unreliable.
611.ch: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
611.q: I tell you, I tell you, I tell you a record if you got it there, Phil, that I, only one that I remember real well when people have asked me the same story many times. The first thing, I didn't even hear the record, some of 'em, till I got to Europe. That was -

611.t: Using sidemen to identify his Oliver and Williams sessions
611.s: Waters says if Cy St. Clair on bass is not on a date he was not there; he also names Cuffey, Ben Whitted and Happy Cauldwell, and says the dates were done while he worked at Small's Paradise.
611.ch: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
611.q: Wait a second, let me give you the names of some, then you compare it with that book. Here's the, here's some of the names I remember real well. The first session we had Cy St. La, Cy St. Clair on bass. And if Cy St. Clair isn't on those records then I wasn't there, because every record that I made…

282.t: Where and when the Sam Morgan records were made
282.s: The Sam Morgan records for Columbia were made in New Orleans, possibly 1926, and Brown heard he was the first recorded bass.
282.q: Oh, I forgot the year now. My, that was in 26. Wasn't that the year? Something along in about that time. Around 26, 25 or 26. When did you make the records, do you remember? Yeah. Yeah. Oh, no.

49.t: Rhythm Kings Victor and OK recording sessions
49.s: He describes the two sessions in New Orleans, Rappolo's high notes, and who played.
49.q: Yeah. The ones they made here, you mean? Uh, uh... August Schillang on drums. Uh... Santo, Rap. Well now they made... They made two sessions here. They made an OK session here and they made a Victor session here. The OK was with Santo, Rap, Paul... Steve Loiskaner, Freddie Newman, piano, and Chink.…

649.t: Identifying Margaret Johnson's titles and the 1926 session
649.s: Interviewer reads titles; Palmer recognises the Delaney songs and confirms he played on the 1926 Victor titles.
649.q: I think James wrote this. I think James B. Johnson wrote it. James B. Johnson. Yeah, I think he did, yeah. Papa and Mama's All Alone.

881.t: Disputed record credits and the 1926 sessions
881.s: They check discographical errors, recording with Richard M. Jones and Louis Russell, and how he got dates for his band.
881.ch: Theater work, first jobs and recording credits
881.q: Well, that's all I was asking. I mean, this Dr. Vollmer, he comes to Chicago. Yeah. Right now, he's trying to correct some of those, some of the errors, you know. Because any time you were taking, talk to different people, they'll have different versions. You understand what I'm talking about?…

51.t: The Spikes Brothers Sunshine session with Dink Johnson
51.s: Ory recalls Fred Washington and Dink Johnson, padding for Dink's foot tapping, and the four sides including Ory's Creole Trombone.
51.q: Dink Johnson. Yeah. Dink Pat his feet so loud, we got a pillar, and then we stood up on a pillar, and the pillar wouldn't do so we got a mattress.

715.t: King Oliver and Williams's blues-contest recordings
715.s: Oliver sometimes recorded with Williams; Williams hired trumpeters for blues contest winners and chose men by results; Allen names the bands he worked with.
715.q: Well he was about anything class way man, King Oliver had something in there to do, he'd come to record it. Whenever he come in time, he'd make some recordings with his band. And most of the time King Oliver made his own band so he didn't have to have nobody. When Clarence was going to make…

25.s: Taylor recalls the Keppard date: Stockyard Blues was his, with Camel on piano, Vinson on trombone, a twelve-piece band and Johnny Dodds on clarinet.
25.q: Yeah, well, Stockyard Blues, that's mine. I just simply had my, played over on the Zillophone and Freddie, got the boys together. And, you know, it didn't take very long before they fall in. Yes.

229.t: 1925 Sonny Clay and 1926 Reb Spikes records
229.s: Redd lists personnel and tunes for the Sonny Clay Plantation Orchestra record and the Reb Spikes sides including Sheffield's Blues.
229.q: MS. REDD: 1925, Andrew Blakeney recorded with the Sonny Clay's Plantation Orchestra in Los Angeles, on Vocalian Label, 1000. This was a 78 disc. The personnel included Ernest Coycault, first trumpet; W.B. Woodman, trombone; Leonard Davidson, clarinet; and James Carson, clarinet and tenor sax; Louis…

9.t: Recording with Luis Russell and King Oliver
9.s: Russell recorded under everyone's name; Holmes made 'Tight Like That', 'Savoy Shout' and 'Call of the Freaks' without knowing titles, plus Oliver dates with Metcalf.
9.q: : ...King Oliver and different ones. Yeah, Russell was recording for everybody, and under everybody's name. Red Allen's name and Higgenbotham's name, and... everybody's name but mine -- he never had me down on those recording dates.

27.t: The one King Oliver recording date, July 1932
27.s: Phillips recalls the Vocalion session for Sweet Like This and Mule-Faced Blues, its full personnel including Tiny Taylor and King Oliver on trumpet, and that nothing was released.
27.q: Yes. Sam Allen and Francis Whitby and Jack Holt were the saxophone section. Sam Allen played first alto, Whitby played tenor, and Jack Holt played third alto. Arthur Williams, trumpet. Pete Jones, trombone. I was on the other trumpet. It had Eddie Anderson on bass horn -- tuba. Bernie Cobbs on…

18.s: His first record was King Oliver's date in New York, where Oliver could not play and Louis Metcalf took the trumpet part.
18.ch: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
18.q: 1928 right here in New York but he couldn't play. He had pyorrhea and Louis Metcalf played the trumpet part. That was the first recording ever I made in my life.

72.s: Welburn and Moore sort out personnel and tunes for Oliver's Victor sessions, including that Moore played on 'Too Late'; Carroll Dickerson led the band.
72.ch: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
72.q: They've got that thing all screwed up. I was on "Too Late."

386.t: Recording with Mayo Williams' portable equipment in 1929 and the Four Quarters
386.s: He recalls recording in a furniture store's rug department in Dallas and the 'Sam Price and His Four Quarters' date.
386.ch: Decca, Cow Cow Blues and royalties
386.q: Bert something. But I'll get his name for you. I'll give you his name. And I'd had a guy named Percy Darenbourg? playing the guitar. He's a New Orleans guy that I'd met...

387.t: Recording Remember in the Padded Cell, Chicago
387.s: Love Song to a Chambermaid and Remember; the padded Chicago studio.
387.q: in June, because I had made arrangements before that, to get ready for that. "Remember" I think was already in the works in the autumn of '36, and recorded in '37; that's true. I remember it well, in Chicago in the Padded Cell.

74.t: The 1928 recording and the Gilded Kisses trio
74.s: Corrects the record list: the trio on Gilded Kisses was Mosley, Stuff Smith and John Fielding.
74.ch: Trent's band: touring, sidemen and breakup
74.q: We worked it out. The band had amazing musicians. Just to think that early in life and nobody to listen to, it came naturally, it came natural with these guys. We worked that thing out. Sometimes I think back myself and wonder how we did it. On this first recording here in 1928, they made a little…

97.t: Discography questions: 1924 Paramount, Black Swan 1921, Elmer Chambers
97.s: Albertson reads names of singers and sessions; Scott corrects dates and says Chambers preceded him with Henderson.
97.q: How could they get me there? I wasn't with Fletcher in '21. No, there's a mistake there someplace. '21.
